low.assumptions: 2%/yr rates, 0.7%/yr panel wear, VPP ends after 2030, 3c exports after NEM 2

base.assumptions: 3.5%/yr rates, 0.5%/yr panel wear, VPP continues, 5c exports after NEM 2

high.assumptions: historical rate trend, 0.4%/yr panel wear, VPP continues, 7c exports after NEM 2

notes: Actuals/model through Oct 2026 and the Oct 2026 - Oct 2027 forecast, then one projected year at a time.
Grid-only cost = the same electricity use on E-TOU-D (PG&E delivery + Valley Clean Energy generation), rising with rates.

With solar under NEM 2: Base Services Charge + true-up grid fees, minus Climate Credits, the Valley Clean Energy surplus payout and VPP payouts; panel wear first shrinks the yearly surplus, then adds grid purchases at retail.
After NEM 2 ends (~Sep 2041): assumed to move to net billing: grid imports at full retail, exports credited at a low flat rate.
Electricity use is held at today's level. No discounting in the main figures (present value at 3%/yr shown separately).

Not included: battery or inverter replacement, panel repairs, insurance or property-tax effects. The Powerwall 3s installed in July 2026 carry Tesla's 10-year warranty (to ~2036); a replacement after that, if needed, would reduce the savings.
life25.series_note: grid = cumulative grid-only cost; solar = net system cost + cumulative net electricity with solar; savings = grid - solar (negative before payback)

assumptions: Savings = cost of the same electricity without solar + Powerwall (E-TOU-D at each date's rates) minus the actual net cost (PG&E bills and true-up + VCE settlement - VPP payouts).

Installed Aug 2021; savings counted from the start of operation (Sep 3, 2021) using the Tesla daily data. Sep 2021 - Oct 2022 predates the PG&E interval data and VCE/VPP figures: its actual net cost is pro-rated from the first full true-up year.

Oct 2026 - Oct 2027 uses the next-year forecast; after that, the base case of the 25-year model (3.5%/yr rate increases, 0.5%/yr panel wear, NEM 2 ending ~2041; no battery replacement, no discounting).
Savings are spread evenly over the days of each period; recovered-to-date pro-rates the current true-up year.
